vulnerability.name: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf
vulnerability.description: picomatch: ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs (original range: all versions up to 4.0.7). GitHub WITHDREW this advisory on 2026-11-18 as 'not a security issue' (the upstream view: a glob pattern is trusted input).

statements.status_notes: Checked 2026-11-21 (plan W0, closed by W3). Advisory state: withdrawn by GitHub on 2026-11-18 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf), and `npm audit` on the packed CLI reports 0 vulnerabilities; scanners that have not caught up may still list it. picomatch reaches the CLI only through fast-glob -> micromatch (packages/cli/src/utils/fs.ts calls fast-glob; ShipGuard never calls picomatch itself). The scan patterns are the constant '**/*' and the built-in default ignore list. The one policy-controlled route, src/core/ignore.ts selfArtifactIgnorePatterns() (policy values report.output and history.path), now escapes glob characters (fast-glob escapePath) before the pattern reaches fast-glob, so a repository cannot inject an extglob such as +(*a). ignore.paths from the policy do not reach picomatch (they go through minimatch 11, literal entries escaped). Evidence: packages/cli/tests/gate/ignore-escape.test.ts; packages/cli/tests/release/gates-files.test.ts keeps this status and the code in step. Pinned: picomatch 2.3.2 (runtime, via micromatch; the newest 2.x) and 4.0.4 (dev tooling only) in pnpm overrides.
